The generalized wetlands map does not represent the boundaries of jurisdictional wetlands within Pickens County, Georgia and cannot serve as a substitute for a delineation of wetland boundaries by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, as required by Section 404 of the Clean Water Act, as amended. Any local government action under this article does not relieve the landowner from federal or state permitting requirements.
(Res. of 12-29-2000, § 1)

If the corps determines that wetlands are present on the proposed development site, the local permit or permission will not be granted until a section 404 permit or letter of permission is issued.

754:
Absorption field areas are defined as a minimum of 4,000 square feet useable soils area per bedroom (2,500 square feet per bedroom for initial absorption field plus 2,000 square feet per bedroom for replacement absorption field), or a minimum of 4,000 square feet useable soils per 150 gallons per day of wastewater for commercial and similar structures; these areas may be considered for reduction in size by installing both the initial and replacement absorption fields at the same time, but in no case shall the replacement area be smaller than required for a conventional absorption field system. Where position of structures, width of lots, slope or other characteristics of properties will make future access for replacement or repair of systems very difficult or impossible, both the initial absorption fields and replacement absorption fields will be installed at the same time. Complex slope patterns dissected by rock, deep gullies and ravines are not acceptable for absorption field areas. If larger homes, more bedrooms, swimming pools, tennis courts, outbuildings and other appurtenances are proposed to be constructed or if trees would interfere with installation of an on-site sewage management system, the Pickens County Board of Health will require larger lots to assure useable soil areas. Absorption field areas must remain undisturbed until septic system installation except for clearing of trees and underbrush; no unapproved grading or similar disturbance of soils is permitted except for foundation footings and other activities associated with home construction.
Conventional absorption field system means a traditionally used on-site sewage management system whose absorption field is composed of perforated pipe surrounded by gravel or stone.
Commercial lot means real estate property that is used for business activities whether or not for profit.
GPAD means gallons of sewage effluent applied per acre per day through on-site sewage management absorption fields.
Individual water supply system means a system of piping, pumps, tanks or other facilities utilizing groundwater to supply a single-family dwelling.
Lot means a portion of a subdivision or any other parcel of land, intended as a unit for transfer of ownership, or for development, or both, and shall not include any part of the right-of-way of a street or road. The following land areas are not considered as a part of any lot when calculating the required minimum lot size: rights-of-way of roads, easements (such as power line, pipe line, other utility or adjacent property egress) that exclude installation of an on-site sewage management system, bodies of water, land within 50 feet of a lake, river, stream, wetland, springhead not used for drinking water, or other bodies of water and similar limiting factors.
Maximum daily sewage flow means 600 GPAD when a lot is served by an individual water supply system, and 1,200 GPAD when served by a public water supply system.
Multi-residential means a classification of housing where multiple separate housing units for residential inhabitants are contained within one building or several buildings within one complex and piece of property. A common form is an apartment building or condominium. This definition does not include two-family structures (duplex) or two separate family residential structures on one property.
Onsite sewage management system means a sewage management system other than a public or community sewage treatment system, whether serving single or multiple buildings, mobile homes, recreational vehicles, residences or other facilities designed or used for human occupancy or congregation. It includes conventional septic tank systems and privies, as well as alternative onsite sewage management systems approved by the local health authority.
On-site wastewater treatment system means an advanced alternative wastewater treatment system approved by the state department of public health and that produces an effluent meeting the current ANSI/NSF Standard No. 40 for Residential Wastewater Treatment Systems.
Other lots mean properties not used for family residential, commercial or family multi-residential purposes and may include institutions, schools, camps, churches, rehabilitation or treatment operations, transient facilities and similar.
Percolation rate is defined as the time, expressed in minutes per inch, required for water to seep into unsaturated soil at a constant rate.
Public water supply system means a system for the provision of piped water to the public for human consumption, if such system has at least 15 service connections, or regularly serves an average of at least 25 individuals daily, at least 60 days out of the year as regulated by the Georgia Department of Natural Resources, Georgia Rules for Safe Drinking Water, Chapter 391-3-5.
Slope is defined as the vertical distance, or difference in height, between two points on the ground surface divided by the horizontal distance between these two points expressed as a percentage. The Pickens County Board of Health recognizes that a lot may have different slopes in different areas with varying topography; in this context, the size of a lot is determined by the slope where the initial absorption field and replacement field areas are likely to be or can be located. In questionable circumstances the larger lot size shall be required.
(Res. of 10-19-2017(2), § 1(Exh. A))

a. With public water supply system and on-site sewage management system or on-site wastewater treatment system: 65,340 square feet (one and a half acres) with a minimum 150 feet lot width;
b. With individual water supply system and on-site sewage management system: 108,900 square feet (two and a half acres) with a minimum 150 feet lot width.
(Res. of 10-19-2017(2), § 1(Exh. A))
757:
Proposed commercial and multi-residential property sizes will be determined by the maximum daily sewage flow for proposed structures on properties and lots with slopes of 25 percent or less and percolation rates of 60 minutes per inch or less.
Properties served by a public water supply system may apply 1,200 GPAD.
Properties served by an individual water supply system may apply 600 GPAD.
Commercial and multi-family residential properties with slopes greater than 25 percent and/or percolation rates greater than 60 minutes per inch shall be increased proportionally in size. Required minimum areas within properties for on-site management absorption fields will be based on 4,000 square feet useable soils per bedroom (2,000 square feet initial and 2,000 square feet replacement area) for apartments and other multi-family residential properties, and 4,000 square feet useable soils per 150 gallons of wastewater for commercial and similar properties.
Example: A proposed business will have a public water supply system and will generate 5,000 gallons of wastewater per day. With public water the maximum sewage flow is 1,200 gallons per day per acre. To determine the acreage of the lot needed, use the following formula:
5,000 gal/day divided by 1,200 gal/acre/day = 4.17 acres
NOTE: This does not mean that four and seventeen one-hundredths acres must be reserved for the septic system but that the entire property must be at least four and seventeen one-hundredths acres. However, enough suitable land area must be left within a property for the initial system and replacement system after buildings, paved areas, and appurtenances; minimum areas within properties for absorption fields equal 5,000 square feet useable soils per bedroom, and 5,000 square feet useable soils per 150 gallons wastewater per day for commercial and similar structures (2,500 square feet/bedroom for initial system plus 2,500 square feet for replacement system.) Reserved areas for initial and replacement systems may be reduced by an approved site plan for the initial and replacement systems, or by installing both the initial and replacement systems.
Example: A business will be served by an individual well (non-public system) and generates 5,000 gallons of wastewater per day. In this case the maximum sewage flow is only 600 gallons per acre per day.
5,000 gal/day divided by 600 gal/acre/day = 8.33 acres
Example: A residential property owner has a lot of eight tenths of an acre served by public water and wishes to build a six-bedroom home. Each bedroom requires 150 gallons per day x six bedrooms = 900 gallons per day. 900 gal/day divided by 1,200 gal/acre/day = seventy-five one hundredths of an acre. The property owner can build a six-bedroom home if soil areas are sufficient and suitable. If the property were served by an individual well or other non-public supply, the lot would have to be one and one half acres.
Where existing commercial and multi-residential properties are limited by land area, the property owners may propose on-site wastewater treatment systems and nitrogen reduction technologies for consideration by the county environmental health department.

1000:
The purpose of this article is to provide a process for applicants to petition the board of commissioners of Pickens County on behalf of affected properly owners for the creation of special capital improvement districts, within which, qualified capital improvements would be made through authorized qualified capital improvement projects, which are funded, in whole or in part, by special fees, assessments and/or ad valorem taxes that would be levied on the affected property owners.
(Ord. of 8-19-2024, § 1(Exh. A))
1001:
(a) Affected property owner, for the purposes of this article, means an owner of a property lying within a proposed special capital improvement district put forward by an applicant or within a special capital improvement district created by the board of commissioners.
(b) Applicant, for purposes of this article, means an affected property owner that petitions for the creation of a special capital improvement district.
(c) Qualified capital improvements, for the purposes of this article, means capital improvements with a useful life of ten years or more, made by new construction or other action, which specially benefits all real property within a special capital improvement district, either by increasing the service capacity available to the properties, thereby increasing the marketability or market value of the properties, or by providing other special benefits as determined by the board of commissioners.
Qualified capital improvements shall include, but are not limited to, road paving, road surfacing, sidewalks, curbs, gutters, stormwater control structures, water lines, traffic control devices, and lighting fixtures.
Qualified capital improvements shall not include sanitary sewers.
(d) Qualified capital improvement project, for the purposes of this article, means a project undertaken to make qualified capital improvements to public properly in a special capital improvement district which is funded, in whole or in part by special fees, assessments and/or ad valorem taxes levied on affected property owners.
(e) Project costs, for the purposes of this article, means all costs incurred to undertake and complete a qualified capital improvement project in conformity with all relevant standards, including, but not limited to, planning, design, engineering, construction, land acquisition, land improvement, and administrative costs.
(f) Special capital improvement district, for the purposes of this article, means a district created by the board of commissioners pursuant to Article IX, Section II, Paragraph VI(c) of the Constitution of the State of Georgia, comprised of residential parcels within an existing residential subdivision or comprised of property lying within a discrete and definable land use intensity district used for purposes other than residential use, in which qualified capital improvement projects are undertaken to make qualified capital improvements.
(Ord. of 8-19-2024, § 1(Exh. A))
1002:
(a) Only a publicly owned qualified capital improvement project shall be eligible to be conducted in a special capital improvement district.
(b) Qualified capital improvements must be constructed on public property in order for the qualified capital improvement project to be eligible to be conducted a special capital improvement district.
(c) No proposed qualified capital improvement project shall be considered by the board of commissioners until the private property necessary to complete the proposed qualified capital improvements project is offered for dedication to the county by the applicable affected property owners in writing and in the form and manner required by the public works director.
(Ord. of 8-19-2024, § 1(Exh. A))
1003:
The steps by which an applicant can petition the board of commissioners for the creation of a special capital improvement district are as follows:
(a) An applicant may petition for the creation of a special capital improvement district pursuant this article by filing an application for a preliminary petition therefor with the public works director. See section 41-6.
(b) If the public works director determines that the application is complete, he or she shall develop a preliminary cost estimate for the proposed qualified capital improvement project and provide to the applicant, within 40 calendar days of the receipt of the application, the preliminary cost estimate and the preliminary petition to be completed by the applicant. See section 41-7.
(c) The applicant shall then have 40 calendar days from the issuance of the preliminary petition to complete the preliminary petition by obtaining the signatures of at least 80 percent of the affected property owners and to return the completed preliminary petition to the public works director. See section 41-7.
(d) Upon the timely return of the completed preliminary petition, the public works director shall verify the required signatures and determine whether the proposed project will require additional preliminary steps prior to the issuance of the final petition, including, but not limited to, the dedication of necessary private property, the completion of preliminary studies, reports, or plans and the procurement of additional cost estimates. See section 41-8.
(e) After the verification of the signatures of affected property owners and the completion of any required additional preliminary steps, the public works director shall issue the final petition to the applicant, if all requirements concerning the preliminary petition are satisfied. See section 41-8.
(f) After the issuance of the final petition, the applicant shall have 40 calendar days to obtain the signatures of at least 80 percent of the affected property owners on the final petition and to provide the completed final petition to the public works director. See section 41-8.
(g) As soon as possible after verification of the signatures on the final petition, the public works director shall submit the final petition to the board of commissioners together with estimated costs, construction timelines, funding details and any other information and recommendations as the public works director may deem appropriate. See section 41-8.
(h) As scheduling allows, the board of commissioners shall consider the final petition and exercise its sole discretion as to whether the special capital improvement district will be created, what qualified capital improvement project will be undertaken and what funding sources will be used to fund the project, including to what degree and in what amount special fees, assessments and/or ad valorem taxes will be levied on the affected property owners. See section 41-9.
(Ord. of 8-19-2024, § 1(Exh. A))
1004:
Neither the filing of an application for a petition, nor the submission of a preliminary petition or a final petition nor the expenditure of funds in furtherance of any application or petition will establish any rights in favor of the applicant or any affected property owner with regard to any duties or obligations of Pickens County, its board of commissioners, its other officials, or its employees.
(Ord. of 8-19-2024, § 1(Exh. A))
1005:
(a) Applicants as defined in this article may submit an application to the public works director for a preliminary petition to create a special capital improvement district.
(b) Applications for preliminary petitions shall be considered on a first-come-first-serve basis and only one application shall be considered at any time for a single residential subdivision, or a single discrete and definable land use intensity district used for purposes other than residential use.
(c) The application for a preliminary petition must include the following:
(1) A description of the property to be included within the proposed special capital improvement district.
(2) A concise and clear description of the qualified capital improvements being sought to be made in the proposed special capital improvement district.
(3) A signed acknowledgment by the applicant agreeing that:
a. All aspects of the petition for and creation of any special capital improvement district and of the undertaking and funding of any corresponding qualified capital improvement project to make qualified capital improvements are governed by applicable provisions of the Code of Ordinances of Pickens County, Georgia.
b. Neither the filing of an application for a petition, nor the submission of a preliminary petition or a final petition nor the expenditure of funds in furtherance of any application or petition shall establish any rights in favor of the applicant or any affected property owner with regard to any duties or obligations of Pickens County, its board of commissioners, its other officials, or its employees.
c. The public works director is authorized to require applicants to supplement their preliminary petition by providing, at the applicant's own cost, any additional information, studies, reports, or plans deemed necessary by the public works director as a condition precedent to further consideration of an application, preliminary petition or final petition.
d. The public works director retains the sole discretion to determine what information, studies, reports, and plans are required for each proposed qualified capital improvement project on a case-by-case basis.
e. The public works director retains the sole discretion to prioritize applications and petitions for the creation of any special capital improvement district and the undertaking of corresponding proposed qualified capital improvements considering various relevant factors determined by him or her.
f. Only a publicly owned qualified capital improvement project shall be eligible to be conducted in a special capital improvement district.
g. Qualified capital improvements must be constructed on public property in order for the qualified capital improvement project to be eligible to be conducted a special capital improvement district.
h. No proposed qualified capital improvement project shall be considered by the board of commissioners until the private property necessary to complete the proposed qualified capital improvements project is offered for dedication to the county by the applicable affected property owners in writing and in the form and manner required by the public works director.
i. The board of commissioners retains the sole discretion as to whether any special capital improvement district shall be created, what qualified capital improvement project will be undertaken therein and what funding sources will be used to fund the project, including to what degree and in what amount special fees, assessments and/or ad valorem taxes will be levied on the affected property owners.
(4) In prioritizing applications and petitions for the creation of any special capital improvement district and the undertaking of corresponding proposed qualified capital improvements, the public works director shall consider the following factors in addition to any other factors deemed relevant by him or her.
a. The date of application.
b. Anticipated costs of the proposed qualified capital improvement project.
c. Availability and sources of funding.
d. Expected benefits of the proposed qualified capital improvement project.
e. The initial level of support for the proposed qualified capital improvement project as evidenced by the percentage of qualifying signatures by affected property owners.
f. Apparent difficulties in obtaining property and access rights that would be required to enable the proposed qualified capital improvement project.
(Ord. of 8-19-2024, § 1(Exh. A))

(a) If the public works director determines that a preliminary petition has been timely returned with the required percentage of verified signatures, he or she shall determine whether the proposed qualified capital improvement project will require additional preliminary steps prior to the issuance of the final petition, such as the dedication of private property or the completion of preliminary studies, reports, or plans in order to develop a project plan, timeline, and cost estimate for the proposed qualified capital improvement project.

1008:

(a) Any person who shall do or engage in any of the following acts or things within the unincorporated area of Pickens County, Georgia, shall be guilty of disorderly conduct and shall be punished in accord with the provisions of this section. (3) Striking or attempting to strike another.
(4) Assemble or congregate with another or with others to cause, provoke, or engage in any fight or brawl.
(5) Collect in bodies or in crowds and engage in unlawful activities and fail to withdraw from the assembly on being lawfully commanded to do so by a peace officer.

1024:
The commissioner of the county has determined that an increase in juvenile violence and crime by persons under the age of 16 in the county can be avoided. It is known that persons under the age of 16 are particularly susceptible by their lack of maturity and experience to participate in unlawful activity and to be victims of older perpetrators of crime; and that there has been a significant breakdown in the supervision and guidance normally provided by parents for minors resulting in crimes and other unacceptable behavior, such as illiteracy, juvenile pregnancy, increased school drop-out rate. The county has an obligation to provide for the protection of minors from each other and from other persons, for the enforcement of parental control over and responsibility for children, for the protection of the general public, and for the reduction of the incidence of juvenile criminal activities which are not easily controlled by existing laws and ordinances. The commissioner of the county has determined a truancy ordinance for those of school age will be in the interest of the public health, safety, and general welfare and will help to attain the foregoing objectives and to diminish the undesirable impact of such conduct on the citizens of the county and will promote the public good, safety and welfare. Parental responsibility for the whereabouts of children is the accepted norm and legal sanctions to enforce such responsibility have had demonstrated effectiveness in many communities. The commissioner of the county has determined that a truancy ordinance will increase parental responsibility for minors within their control and decrease minor delinquency.
(Res. of 6-23-2011, § B(42-3.1))

1044: There is hereby created a Department of Parks and Recreation for Pickens County, referred to in this article as the department of parks and recreation, to be organized and funded through and under the office of commissioner of the county. The department of parks and recreation shall have the responsibility and duty of providing and maintaining a parks and recreation program for the citizens of the county. The department of parks and recreation shall consist of a director of parks and recreation and a parks and recreation advisory board.
1045:
There is hereby created the office of director of parks and recreation; such director of parks and recreation to be employed by the commissioner of the county and to serve at the discretion of such commissioner.
(1) The director of parks and recreation shall organize and manage a parks and recreation program.
(2) The director of parks and recreation may employ personnel necessary for maintenance of the program with the approval of the commissioner.
(3) The director of parks and recreation shall prepare and submit to the commissioner an annual budget for the program and a quarterly report of all income and expenditures for such program.
(Res. of 2-1-1993, § II)
1046:
There is hereby created a Parks and Recreation Advisory Board for Pickens County, Georgia, referred to in this article as the parks and recreation advisory board.
(1) The parks and recreation advisory board shall consist of nine members, appointed by the commissioner of the county, who shall serve one-year terms beginning January 1 and ending December 31 and who can be reappointed.
(2) The parks and recreation advisory board shall meet regularly, and at the call of the director of parks and recreation, to advise and assist in planning and implementing the parks and recreation program; to advise and assist in the preparation of the annual budget and the quarterly reports of income and expenditures; to assist in maintaining an inventory and accounting of all property utilized or owned by the department of parks and recreation; and to do such other things as necessary for the department of parks and recreation.
(3) The parks and recreation advisory board shall select from its members a chairperson to preside and a secretary to keep accurate minutes and records. The director of parks and recreation shall act as treasurer. The parks and recreation advisory board may select other officers and committees from its members or the general public as it deems necessary.
(Res. of 2-1-1993, § III; Res. of 2-12-98)
1047:
Any accounts maintained by the department of parks and recreation separate from the general fund of the office of commissioner shall be in a banking institution designated by the commissioner and shall require the signatures of the director of parks and recreation and one other member of the parks and recreation advisory board. Any such account shall be in the name of "Department of Parks and Recreation of Pickens County, Georgia" and have an address of the office of commissioner.
(Res. of 2-1-1993, § IV)
